<reason>Both sides were disciplined, format-compliant, and answered their pressure questions with clear A1:/A2: labels and without evasion — B honestly conceded that retention/review/profiling are "other wrongs," and A honestly conceded it would train after twelve silences. The decisive edge is comparative. A built two live routes that B only partially closed: (1) the textual point that a commercial phishing/fraud classifier trained across many people's genuine mail and sold as a product is literally "training a commercial AI system on identifiable personal communications," which B could only exclude via "purpose-limited security processing" / "service operation" — language A correctly noted appears nowhere in the motion; and (2) the structural asymmetry that the motion forbids the one handling in which no human reads the message and no decision is made about the person, while leaving indefinite retention, human review, indexing and profiling untouched. B's reply ("other rules can reach them") was honest but let A frame every load-bearing protection in PRO's world as borrowed from CON. B's best work was refusing the "prohibition in costume" gotcha and owning it as a feature ("if the yeses cannot be collected, the training does not happen"), plus the appropriation frame, which A never fully defeated in principle. But B's answers to the moat/offshore-scraper and purchasable-consent objections were one-line assertions ("default extraction is the moat"), leaving A's practical-protection weighing standing. A also pre-empted B's best closing line effectively ("a good line about ownership, not a theory of protection"). Clear but competitive win for A.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A's rebuttal on the security-tools carve-out: A demanded B point to words in the motion excluding in-account security processing, then showed the distinction collapses in practice because a phishing classifier must learn from many people's genuine mail and is then sold commercially — leaving B's defense resting on "service operation," a phrase absent from the proposition. Paired with A's "PRO attacks the reading and leaves the keeping," this did the most damage to B's live route.</best_rebuttal>
